messages:
alex: heads-up: we started seeing duplicated SSE events for some long-lived connections when the router table changes. noticed in prod about 14:07 UTC. :bug:
jamie: do you mean the same stream id got replayed twice or two different connections?
sana: I saw the console show the same session twice under different worker shards — looked like a fanout after a shard split.
alex: exactly. root cause seems to be when a multiplexed connection (multiple logical streams per conn) resumes we send a resume request to a shard based on stale routing and it gets forwarded to both new and old shard during transition. both deliver the buffered events.
liam: ugh. any logs? can you paste the resume headers?
alex: log snippet: `INFO resume_req id=rs_42 stream=ux-chat user=acct-9 routing_hint=shard-12 forwarded_to=[shard-12,shard-17]` then two `deliver_event` lines for same `event_seq`
jamie: if the router forwards to both, we should be deduping on deliver with `resume_id`. I thought we had that, but maybe it only covered single-stream resume.
sana: looks like dedupe only checks `client_conn_id` + `seq`. for multiplexed streams the router can change mapping and `client_conn_id` differs.
liam: short-term: we can add an opaque `X-Resume-Id` that is stable per logical stream across routing changes. serverside dedupe by `X-Resume-Id + seq`.
alex: proposed header: `X-Resume-Id: <uuid>` added to resume and resume-replies. example curl: `curl -H "X-Resume-Id: rs-42" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://stream.redwood/api/v1/resume`
ops-bot: automated-test-failure: stream-resume-dedupe (flaky) also flagged in CI 5m ago
jamie: good to know. we should also fix router to avoid simultaneous forwarding. make consistent-hash sticky for a small TTL during rollouts to avoid split-brain fanout.
sana: agree. sticky TTL = 30s should be enough to avoid transient duplicates during rollout windows. update rollout UX to show shard migration windows in the console so SREs can pick low-traffic times.
liam: telemetry: we currently only emit `resume_attempt` and `resume_forward_count`. need `resume_dedupe_hit` and `resume_duplicate_deliveries` metrics to detect regressions. add a p99 of duplicate_deliveries per tenant.
jamie: implementation plan: 1) server dedupe on `X-Resume-Id+seq` (feature flag). 2) router sticky mapping TTL + no-parallel-forwarding during migration. 3) console: expose live shard-migration overlay and warn when migration in progress. 4) add metrics + dashboard panel and alert if duplicates > 0.1% traffic.
alex: rough rollout: enable flag for 10% of traffic tomorrow, monitor `resume_duplicate_deliveries`. can someone own the canary? :eyes:
sana: I'll own canary and dashboard. will add query to console: `sum(rate(resume_duplicate_deliveries[5m])) by (tenant)` and a table widget.
liam: I'll do the router change and a unit-test for forwarding behavior.
jamie: I'll add server dedupe; need to pick header name and update SDKs. also update docs with header semantics.
alex: small note: ensure quota billing remains idempotent — if we dedupe delivery we must not refund already-charged tokens or double-charge. billing team will need to be in the loop.
sana: pinging @billing on this thread — can you confirm how to reflect dedupe in per-tenant token accounting?
ops-bot: @billing not a member of this channel. (automated)
jamie: tagging billing alias in the ticket.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: router-change branch -> staging in 10m
alex: thanks. let's sync after canary starts and iterate. :thumbsup:
